This guide explains what the licensing portal is, when Support or your CSM asks you to re-login your license, and how to reset a forgotten license password. Applies to Sisense Linux, cloud and on-prem. What my.sisense.com is My Sisense is the licensing portal where you view your account and license details. Reach it at my.sisense.com/login and log in with your license email and password. From there you can see your license overview, add a user to the license, generate an offline key, and manage license users (change password, delete user). When Support or your CSM asks you to re-login your license Sometimes Support or Customer Success will ask you to re-login the license in the Sisense app — for example after a renewal or when the instance still shows an old or expired license. To do this: In Sisense Application, click Admin . Open License Utilization (System Administrators only). Scroll to the Change License section. Enter your license email and license password. Click Save so the instance picks up the current license. Important: the password this screen asks for is the same one you use on my.sisense.com — not your Sisense app user password. What to do if you don't remember your license password You can reset it on the license portal, then use the new password in the app: Go to my.sisense.com/login and click Forgot Password . Enter the license email address. A Reset Password email is sent — follow it to set a new password. Log in to my.sisense.com with the new password to confirm it works. In Sisense, go to Admin → License Utilization → Change License , enter the license email and the new password, and click Save . Conclusion: my.sisense.com is your license portal, separate from your Sisense app login. When asked to re-login your license in Admin → License Utilization → Change License, use your my.sisense.com credentials. If you don't remember that password, reset it with Forgot Password on my.sisense.com — the same reset lets you into the portal and lets you re-login the license in the app. References/Related Content: My Sisense (Licensing Application) — docs.sisense.com/main/SisenseLinux/my-sisense.htm Managing Your License Utilization — docs.sisense.com/main/SisenseLinux/license-utilization.htm Activating Sisense on Linux — docs.sisense.com/main/SisenseLinux/activating-sisense-on-linux.htm Disclaimer : This post outlines a potential custom workaround for a specific use case or provides instructions regarding a specific task. Best Practices Understanding pivot table sorting and how it differs from table widget sorting Introduction: Sorted a pivot column but the values still look unordered? The is a good chance that sort is actually working as intended — pivots sort within row groups, not across the whole widget. Learn why this happens and how to get the order you expect. Applies to Sisense Linux, both Cloud and on-prem. Understand why pivot sorting looks like it "isn't working" A pivot table is an aggregating widget. It first arranges its rows by the hierarchy of dimensions in the Rows panel, and a sort is then applied within the lowest level of that grouping — not across every row of the widget. The sort is being applied; it just happens inside each group, so at a glance the column can still look unordered. The rule to remember: in a pivot, sorting only applies to the last level of granularity — the groups within the last row dimension. See it in a worked example Consider a pivot with Contract ID as the leading row dimension, followed by Title , Supplier , Status , and an Expiration Date column, with an ascending sort set on Expiration Date — yet the dates still look unordered. Because Contract ID is the leading dimension and is unique for every contract, each Expiration Date lands in its own single-row group. The ascending sort has no sibling rows to reorder, so the dates keep following the row hierarchy above them. The field type and the ascending setting are both correct — there is simply nothing to sort within each group. If there were multiple members in a group, you would see the sorting applied inside the group.
